chapter.title: Stems
chapter.sub: The room sounded perfect. Four thousand people online heard a different show.
chapter.status: **DRAFT** · scripted from the season map ahead of its production-bible entry · CASE-008 mechanism is the SIGNAL adaptation (Q-004) · IDs provisional

items.text: SEASON 2 · EPISODE 7 · DRAFT  Countdown · Leah and Maya · Level L3 · CASE-008  Graham's launch sounds perfect in the room. Online, four thousand people — and his CEO — are hearing a show nobody approved.  ⚑ RV-52 · Q-004: the stream mechanism is the SIGNAL adaptation; tap-point behavior differs by console. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: The Mix Nobody Approved
items.stakes: Four thousand people online heard a joke from the wings. Graham's CEO is watching from an airport lounge.
items.clock: Fifteen seconds. Then the whole launch.
items.reward: The stream that follows the room's mutes but not its faders. Graham's trust — or at least his silence.

objectives.text: Kill the wings mic online — in fifteen seconds
Figure out who the stream is listening to
Choose the right tap point — now
Prove it on a second pair of ears
Look closer: two things said at 1:20 p.m.

items.rumor: The stream vendor said “you'll never fight the FOH guy.” That was the problem.

items.text: Cold open — “Nobody in the room noticed”

items.alt: A dark launch room: a big LED wall glows with an abstract new product under the word INTRODUCING. A presenter in silhouette stands on stage. The audience fills the frame's bottom edge.
items.caption: Graham's launch. 380 in the room. 4,000 online. His CEO is watching from an airport lounge.

items.alt: Stage left, in the wings: Reid, the co-presenter, laughing with a stagehand, a wireless pack clipped to his belt and its mic on his collar.
items.caption: Reid goes on in twenty minutes. His mic is on. In the room, it's muted.

items.alt: The tech desk at the back of the room. Dante mixes the room, relaxed. Maya, at the stream mixer beside him, presses her headphones to her ears.

bubbles.text: Room's easy. Small room, loud band — I've barely got them in the PA.
Dante. Somebody in the wings is on the stream. Telling a joke.

items.caption: In Maya's headphones: a joke nobody in the room would ever repeat. Four thousand people just heard it.

lines.text: Somebody in the wings is on the stream? Telling a joke?
They never are, when four thousand people hear them.

items.alt: Two phones. One shows the stream's chat filling with alarm and complaints about the band. The other, Graham's, shows a message from the CEO: Who is telling jokes on my launch?
items.caption: Nobody in the room noticed. Everybody online did.

items.prompt: A live mic in the wings is on the stream right now. Fifteen seconds.
items.happening: A co-presenter's mic in the wings is live on the stream, not in the room.
known: ◉ The stream mixer has a WINGS stem
unknown: Why the stream hears a mic the room doesn't
items.risk: Four thousand viewers, a CEO, a product launch — and Reid's reputation.
timeout: The joke finishes. Reid laughs, and so does someone next to him. Online, the clip is already being shared.
In a live leak, the first job is stopping it — with the smallest move.

hints.text: What is the smallest move that stops this one input online?

options.label: Mute that input on the stream mixer
options.result: One button. The wings go silent online. The presenter and band carry on.
options.consequence: The harm stops. You still don't know why the stream heard it.

options.label: Pull the whole stream audio
options.result: Four thousand people lose the presenter, the band, everything.
options.fail: The whole stream for one bad input. The smallest move was one button away.

options.label: Cut the stream to a holding slide
options.result: A beautiful slide. The joke carries on underneath it.
options.consequence: Viewers now see a slide and hear the wings.
options.fail: The problem was audio. You changed the picture.

options.label: Wait — the joke will end on its own
options.result: It ends. Then Reid starts another.
options.consequence: Every second is a clip somebody saves.
options.fail: Not deciding is deciding to broadcast.

items.alt: Dante points at his console: the wings channel's mute button is lit red. Maya looks from it to her stream mixer.

bubbles.text: That mic's been muted for ten minutes. Look — red.
Not on the stream it hasn't.

items.caption: A mute that works in the room and not online. Remember that.

items.alt: Close on the stream mixer: the BAND stem meter pinned red at the top, SPEECH at half, the WINGS stem muted by hand.
items.caption: The wings are muted by hand. The band is still pinned. The presenter is fighting it.

items.alt: Dante pulls the band's group fader down ten decibels. Maya watches her stream mixer's band meter: it doesn't move.

bubbles.text: Band down ten. Anything?
Nothing. The stream doesn't care what your faders do.

items.caption: Mute ignored. Fader ignored.

evidence.label: fader −10 dB · stream band stem unchanged

items.prompt: The joke has stopped online. The band is still pinned. Where do you look?
items.happening: The stream ignores Dante's mute and his faders.

options.label: The stream vendor's patch sheet and the stem sends' tap setting
options.result: The sheet says STREAM STEMS · TAP: INPUT (PRE). The console confirms it: every stem is taken before processing, mute and fader.
options.consequence: You know exactly where the stream is listening.

options.label: Swap Reid's wireless mic
options.result: A new mic, same routing. The stream still ignores Dante's mute.
options.consequence: You replaced the only part that was working perfectly.
options.fail: The mic did its job. The routing decided who heard it.

options.label: Ask the vendor to “fix the stream”
options.result: He's in the loading dock. “Fix what? It's healthy.”
options.consequence: He's right about the encoder and wrong about the mix.

options.label: Restart the encoder to reset its audio
options.result: Sixty seconds of black stream. It comes back with the same mix.
options.consequence: Four thousand people saw the fault get worse.
options.fail: The encoder was faithfully encoding the wrong mix.

items.alt: Flashback to 1:20 p.m.: the stream vendor hands Maya his patch sheet. It reads: stems 1–4 to the stream mixer, tap: input (pre). Independent of the room.

bubbles.text: Stems are pre. The stream's independent of the room — you'll never fight the FOH guy.

items.caption: It's a good template for a multitrack recording. Maya nodded. She never asked what “independent” would cost.

items.title: “Stems are pre.”
items.body: Signed at 1:20 p.m. The box for *who approved the stream mix?* is empty. Maya remembers nodding. She doesn't remember anyone asking.

items.title: The stream isn't listening to Dante.
items.body: Everyone assumed the stream heard the room engineer's mix. It doesn't. The stems are tapped at each channel's input — before the gate, before the mute, before the fader. Dante's mute on Reid's mic never reached the stream; neither did his riding the loud band down. The room and the stream share one console and hear two different shows.
items.label: Test: reason from the tap point before you read on.

items.alt: System View: one console channel strip, input to preamp to gate-EQ-compressor to mute to fader to the room mix. The stream's tap is drawn at the input, before everything.
items.caption: Tapped at the input, the stream hears everything the room engineer silences.

items.label: **Clue Board:** which three clues prove where the stream is listening?

items.sub: Beginner · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Leah and Maya beside a board. Lip sync is voice and lips arriving together. Every box in the picture path adds latency; the audio path usually adds less. So I delay the audio? By the difference. Picture path a hundred twenty milliseconds, audio already twenty: add a hundred. Measured, not by ear.

bubbles.text: Lip sync is voice and lips arriving together. Every box in the picture path adds latency; the audio path usually adds less.
So I delay the audio?
By the difference. Picture path a hundred twenty milliseconds, audio already twenty: add a hundred. Measured, not by ear.

items.caption: Beginner: the term, what it means, the formula — and one worked example out loud.

items.text: 📘 RAY'S NOTEBOOK · BEGINNER  Terms    Lip sync   Whether a speaker's voice and lip movement arrive together.   Latency   Delay a stage adds to a signal.   Formula, variables and a worked example   ƒ FORMULA · Audio delay to match picture  D audio  = L video  − L audio    L video   latency of the picture path, ms  L audio   latency already in the audio path, ms    Worked example.  Picture path 120 ms, audio path already 20 ms: add 120 − 20 = 100 ms of audio delay.
📒 EMPATHIA LEARN FIELDBOOK · MODULE 18 OF 31 · PP. 142–154  PART 9 LIVESTREAMING, COMPUTERS & SOFTWARE  Page 142. Maya: “The stream is a room too. It's just a room full of phones.”

items.label: **Learn it now:** stream tap points and A/V sync.

items.alt: In the wings, Maya quietly explains to Reid that his mic has been on the stream. Reid's hands fly up in horror.

bubbles.text: Your mic's muted in the room. It wasn't online. I'm sorry — that's our routing, not you.
Four thousand people. Oh no. Oh, no.

items.prompt: (white as paper) Four thousand people. That was supposed to be a joke for the crew. Oh no. Oh, no.

options.label: “That's our routing, not you. I'm sorry.”
“Maybe don't tell jokes near a mic.”
options.reply: Thank you. That's very helpful right now.

options.label: (Say nothing. Fix it.)
options.reply: (He stands there, not knowing whether to leave.)

items.title: The first concert on the internet
items.body: On June 24, 1993, a band made up largely of computer researchers played a set in Palo Alto, California, and sent it live — sound and grainy video — over the MBone, an experimental multicast layer of the early internet. Only a few hundred machines could receive it, and the picture ran at a few frames per second. The group was reportedly named Severe Tire Damage. The point wasn't the picture quality: it was that a room's performance could reach people who weren't in the room, and that they might hear something different from the people who were.

items.alt: Back at the desk, alone, Dante reaches across to Maya's console settings and flips the stem sends. On the stream mixer, the band meter falls almost to nothing.

bubbles.text: Easy. Make the stems follow my faders. Now my mutes count too.

items.caption: 2:26 p.m. A trusted hand, a reasonable idea, and one setting changed while Maya was in the wings.

items.alt: In the green room, Leah watches the stream on her phone: the band is playing on screen, but she can hardly hear it.

bubbles.text: Maya — where's the band? On the stream, they're miming. There's no band.

items.caption: Two minutes ago the band was too loud online. Now it's gone.

lines.text: Maya — where's the band? On the stream they're miming.
You fixed it so hard it's gone.

items.alt: Maya, back at the desk, sees what Dante changed.

bubbles.text: I made the stems follow my faders. That's what you wanted, right?
Your band's nearly out of the PA. The room hears them through the air. The stream can't.

items.title: The fix made the stream follow the room.
items.body: Post-fader, the stream inherits the room's balance — and the room's balance is built on sound the stream can't hear. In a small room with a loud band, Dante barely needed them in the PA, so online they all but vanished. Dante's instinct (obey the room engineer) was half right: the stream should obey his mutes, not his faders.
items.label: Test: which tap is half of each?

items.alt: System View: the same channel strip with the tap moved to after the fader; the stream now follows the room's balance.
items.caption: Post-fader: the stream hears only what the room needed from the PA.

items.prompt: 2:27. The band is gone online; the wings mic must stay dead. Choose the tap, now.
items.happening: The stems are post-fader; the band has vanished online.
items.risk: The demo is the product's big moment. Four thousand people and a CEO.
timeout: The demo starts with a silent band online and Dante still pushing faders.
The two wrong taps were both on screen. So was the right one.

hints.text: You want the room's mutes, not the room's faders.

items.lab_label: build the stems: after processing, after the mutes, before the faders.

options.label: Leave it post-fader and push the band up in the room
options.result: The room gets louder than anyone wanted. The stream gets some band back.
options.consequence: You're mixing the room for the stream.
options.fail: Two audiences, one balance: somebody always loses.

options.label: Pre-fader, post-mute, after processing — then balance the stems in headphones
options.result: Mutes and gates apply online; Dante's faders don't. Maya trims the band stem for headphones.
options.consequence: The wings mic stays dead because Dante muted it. The band is back, at a level someone approved.

options.label: Back to input taps; ride every hot mic by hand
options.result: It works, until the next mic Dante mutes and you don't.
options.consequence: A stream that depends on you never blinking.
options.fail: You'd be the mute. For every channel. For the rest of the show.

options.label: Feed the stream the room's main mix
options.result: Room EQ, room balance, almost no band. Worse in headphones.
options.consequence: The stream becomes a microphone in the wrong room.
options.fail: A room mix isn't a stream mix.

items.alt: The stream mixer again: SPEECH strong, BAND healthy in the green, WINGS dead. Maya listens in headphones, one hand on the band stem.
items.caption: Pre-fader, post-mute: the room's mutes count online; the room's faders don't.

items.label: **Route it:** the co-presenter's path to the stream, with the tap in the right place.

items.text: Act III — “A second pair of ears”

items.prompt: The stream sounds right at the desk. How do you prove it?
items.happening: The tap is fixed and balanced at the desk.
timeout: You go back to mixing. Nobody listens to the stream on a phone until tomorrow's recording review.
A fix you haven't heard where the viewers are is a belief.

options.label: The booth confidence monitor
options.result: It sounds fine at the booth.
options.consequence: It shares every stage you just changed.
options.fail: The weakest test: it rides the path you're trying to prove.

options.label: The encoder says “Healthy”
options.result: It does. It said that during the joke too.

options.label: Leah on cellular, headphones, the real stream, a whole song — plus a clap test for sync
options.result: Leah: “Clean. Band's there. Nobody in the wings. But the words come before the lips.”
options.consequence: Proof where the viewers are — and a new fault found by it.

options.label: Watch chat for complaints
options.result: Chat moves on to the product.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #18 · AVERY'S LENS  Monitor what the audience gets  The operator should hear exactly what the audience hears, not a different mix.  Nobody in the room listened to the stream. A stream monitor on real headphones would have caught the wings mic in seconds.

items.alt: Leah in the green room, headphones on, phone in hand, on cellular.

bubbles.text: Clean. Band's back. But the words land before the lips move. Like a badly dubbed film.

items.caption: Proof on an independent path found something the desk couldn't.

items.alt: System View of a clap test: the picture track shows the clap three frames after the sound track shows the clap arriving. Fix: delay audio by the measured gap.
items.caption: The picture is late through the switcher and frame sync. The audio waits — by a measured 40 ms.

items.alt: Leah, still on headphones, gives a thumbs-up; Maya on the phone at the desk.

bubbles.text: Lips match. Song's done. Clean the whole way.
Then it's proven. Stay on through the demo anyway.

evidence.label: stream · cellular · headphones · in sync · 2:36 p.m.

items.alt: After the launch. Graham at the tech desk, jabbing a finger at the stream mixer. Maya stands and takes it.

bubbles.text: Four thousand people. My CEO. A joke from the wings. Who is responsible?
The stream's tap point was wrong, and I checked the room, not the stream. That's on me.

items.caption: Leah, two steps behind, between her biggest client and her crew.

items.alt: Graham's phone buzzes: the CEO writes that it was the best stream they've ever had after 2:15 — and to tell Reid she heard the joke.
items.caption: The joke was Graham's own product lead. The CEO knows. So, now, does Graham.

items.teaser: Graham's phone, face up on the table
items.title: A message from the airport lounge
items.body: *Who was that in the wings?* It's from the CEO. The answer, everyone in the room slowly realizes, is Graham's own product lead. Graham turns the phone over.

items.label: **Service Mode:** run the stream crisis yourself, on a clock.

Dante and Maya pack up the desk.

bubbles.text: I changed your settings while you were in the wings. I shouldn't have.
You found half the answer. Next time, tell me first — then we'd have found all of it together.

lines.text: I changed your settings while you were in the wings.
You found half the answer. Next time tell me first. Then we find all of it.

items.alt: Graham, calm now — oddly calm — faces Leah across the tech desk.

bubbles.text: Fine. Tonight's partner show, the CEO walks on live. You'll add my new product-reveal cue. Tonight.
Tonight? The only hour we have is the pre-show checklist.

items.caption: Graham: “Then that's the hour.” Next: *Doors in Four Cues.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A stream is its own audience. Know where it listens: an input tap ignores the room's mutes; a post-fader tap inherits a balance built for a room. Tap pre-fader, post-mute, after processing, and balance for headphones. Measure sync with a clap and delay the audio to the picture. Prove it with a second listener on an independent path, for longer than a song.

REFLECTION (optional)  · Dante changed a setting to help, and Maya had accepted a template without asking what it cost. Neither was careless; both were alone. When was the last time a helpful change of yours landed on someone who wasn't in the room?  Boundary: this reflection proves nothing about the stream.
